rows.text: The log is strictly append-only: the package holds no code that changes or deletes an activity_events row, and not one writing HTTP route.
The only live writer is AuditEventSubscriber. ActivityService.record and the ACTIVITY_RECORDER token are kept, marked @deprecated, and nobody writes through them.
The log row's primary key equals the source event's id, and the insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — re-delivery never produces a duplicate and never rewrites a row already written.
A row's at equals the event's occurredAt, that is, the fact's logical time rather than its delivery time. created_at is never selected on a read.

toAuditRow is a pure function with no database access; returning null means "not our kind", and an exception means "our kind, but there is nothing to name the subject with". The two outcomes are never conflated.
A row with an empty subject_id is never written: the membership mapper refuses rather than substituting a default.

The actor is lifted off payload.actor into the actor_id, actor_type and actor_email columns and is never duplicated inside meta. Its via — how, not who — is the one part that does land in meta, merged with the kind's own payload rather than replacing it.
Not one mapper carries a secret into meta: no password, no hash, no token value and no token hash. For an API token the field set is given by enumeration rather than by copying the payload wholesale.
The subscriber accepts exactly the kinds listed in FACET_MAPPERS: AUDITED_EVENT_KINDS is its kinds, computed from that same table.
An event of a kind absent from FACET_MAPPERS produces an error nowhere: it is stamped delivered and never reaches the log.

Every audit kind maps from exactly one event kind, with one deliberate exception: user.disabled/user.enabled land on the same audit kinds as member.disabled/member.reactivated, so 62 mappings produce 60 distinct kinds. Which aggregate performed the change is an internal fact; the reader wants "this account was suspended".

A kind is renamed only where the two catalogues historically diverged: member.* to user.*, auth.signed_in/auth.signed_out to user.signed_in/user.signed_out, and api_token.* to token.*. The rest pass straight through.
The subject of a workspace-membership event is the user, not the workspace; the workspace's id travels in meta.workspaceId.

GET /api/activity and /dead-letters are reachable only with a session and only with the activity:read permission; they are unreachable with an external API bearer token. /entries/:id takes a session and content:read, and additionally requires membership of the workspace named in X-Workspace-Id.
All filters intersect with AND, the ?filter= tree included; the absence of filters gives the full set rather than an empty one.
The filterable surface is eight columns; meta and created_at are not in it under any parameters.
The sort column is picked from an allow-list (at, kind), and an id desc tiebreaker is always appended, so pagination is deterministic with identical timestamps.
A pageSize above MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100 is rejected by the server as a 400; the log page clamps the value before sending so that such a refusal is not unrecoverable from the interface.
Search by the actor's address is case-insensitive and escapes LIKE metacharacters.
created_at appears in the API response under no parameters.
The copilot tool is marked readOnly, effect: 'read', surfaces: ['copilot'] and requires the same permission as the route; it is not offered to the MCP surface.
The tool registry is injected as @Optional(): the absence of the copilot and of MCP is a working configuration rather than a startup error.
The package opens no database connection and owns no schema other than activity_events.
The plugin takes no configuration: ActivityPlugin() and forRoot() are called with no arguments.
The admin-side mapper does not substitute for an unparseable timestamp; every datetime attribute goes through activityDateTime and every visible date through intl.formatDate.
Inside the admin package the kind catalogue and the label catalogue cannot diverge: ACTION_MESSAGES is typed as a record keyed by ActivityKind.
A collapsed details panel is removed from the accessibility tree entirely (aria-hidden and inert), so the number of announced table rows equals the number of events.
Without the activity:read permission the admin UI makes no request at all: the hook's enablement equals the permission, and the home panel returns null.
The page does not stay beyond the last page after a filter narrows the result, but neither does it discard a deep ?page=N link before the first response arrives.
The address bar is the single source of truth for every filter and for the page; any filtered state is reproducible from a link.
actor_type is null if and only if actor_id is: an actored row never claims an unknown kind of principal, and an actor that says nothing about its kind is read as a user.

A token's id never reaches a revision's created_by. The audit path and the revision path take the same EventActor and read it differently — revisionActorId yields a user id or nothing — so naming a credential in the log cannot corrupt a version's authorship.

GET /activity/entries/:id returns only rows whose workspace_id equals the open workspace. An entry id from another workspace yields an empty history, never somebody else's; a row with a null workspace is excluded rather than assumed harmless.
The server's AUDIT_KINDS and the admin's ACTIVITY_KINDS are equal as sets, and every declared kind is reachable from some mapper. Both directions are asserted by a unit test that drives every mapper.

auth.sign_in_failed changes nothing a caller can observe: every refusal path still returns the same error after the same single bcrypt comparison and the same one insert, and a failure to record is swallowed rather than turned into a 500.
api_token.used is raised only when last_used_at is actually touched, so a token produces at most one row per LAST_USED_TOUCH_INTERVAL_MS however much traffic it carries.
No severity level blocks a write. The plugin has no path that returns a refusal to a save or a publish; severity is used only for sorting, colouring and filtering.
A rule's condition is stored verbatim as an entry-list filter tree and evaluated through EntryMatchQuery. There is no second condition format in the system.
All three evaluation paths (an event, an explicit recompute, the sweep) end in one EntryMatchQuery and one AlarmFindingStore.reconcile; they differ only in the set of rows examined.
Reconciliation touches only the entries in examined. A one-row pass cannot close findings it did not ask about.
A redelivered event changes nothing but last_seen_at: the upsert on (rule_id, entry_id) is idempotent.
first_seen_at is written on insert only and never updated — the history survives a finding's closing and reopening.
Creating a rule performs a full collection scan before answering; so does editing an enabled rule's filter.
A rule whose filter has stopped parsing is marked broken, excluded from all three evaluation paths and shown in the interface. It never “silently fails to match”.
A failure to evaluate a filter yields null rather than an empty matched set: “we could not check” must not turn into “nothing matched” and close every one of the rule's findings.
A recompute adds the entries the rule flags that the scan window did not see into the examined set — otherwise such a finding stays open forever.
A recompute that hit maxScanEntries writes a warning and does not report a clean scan of a truncated set.
entry.deleted closes an entry's findings and entry.purged deletes them. A soft delete is reversible, a purge is not.
Deleting a rule deletes its findings by a database cascade; a rule cannot be deleted from another workspace (a workspace_id in the DELETE's where).
A rule's name is unique within a workspace at the database level; a violation is translated into a 409 rather than an unhandled driver error.
A rule's content type is immutable: UpdateAlarmRuleDto has no contentType field.
An unregistered type and an ungranted one answer with an identical 404 and an identical message.
Every route requires a session, workspace membership and one of the two permissions; reads take alarms:read, every write takes alarms:manage; every write additionally carries OriginGuard.
The findings list with no explicit ?state= excludes resolved; the per-entry batch always excludes resolved.
The severity breakdown and the list's page are built from one predicate (findingsWhere) and cannot describe different sets.
Muting a finding exists nowhere: no state, no columns, no route, no tab, no row action. Its absence is pinned down by a server test and a browser test.
A configuration with a zero or negative limit is rejected when the plugin is constructed; sweepIntervalMinutes: 0 is a legitimate “do not sweep”.
The reverse pass considers only rules whose filter tree mentions a relation pointing at the changed type, and is bounded by maxDependentsPerEvent on both sides.
The sweep is sequential, coalesces parallel calls onto the one already running, and waits for completion when the module shuts down.
The server package's domain/ layer imports neither @nestjs/* nor drizzle-orm nor class-validator.
Database writes are chunked at 500 rows — below Postgres's bind-parameter ceiling, which would otherwise fail the whole reconciliation.
The alarm editor serialises the condition with relativeDates: true; a relative window stays relative rather than freezing on the date the rule was written.
Saving with not a single condition is impossible: an alarm with no condition would flag every entry in the collection.
Save always sends the filter key; the API reads a missing key as “do not touch”, and clearing the conditions would silently keep the old ones.
A group's heading and count come from the rule's openCount, not from the page of findings beneath it.
Every admin query is disabled (enabled: false) without the corresponding permission; the cache keys contain the workspace id.
The “Checks” column makes no requests while it is hidden (isVisible is threaded into the hook's enabled).
Severity carries at least three encodings: the glyph's shape, the colour and the word. No surface encodes it by colour alone.
The “loading”, “error” and “empty” states are distinguishable on each of the four reading surfaces (the findings list, the rule list, the entry widget, the column cell).
The copilot tool is read-only, declared surfaces: ['copilot'], bounded by the run's workspace, and has no writing counterpart.
readToolFindings never throws: an unrecognised shape yields null and a fallback to the raw payload, a row with an unknown severity is discarded, and the count comes from bySeverity.
The plaintext secret is returned exactly once — in the response to POST /api/api-tokens — and appears in no other response, no event and no log.
The database stores only the secret's SHA-256 and the non-secret lookup_prefix; the secret itself is persisted nowhere.
After the reveal dialog closes, the secret is absent from page state, the mutation cache, the query cache, the DOM, localStorage/sessionStorage and the URL.
No path out of the reveal dialog (button, Esc, backdrop, cross) discards an uncopied secret without an explicit confirmation.

A token's workspace set is non-empty at issue: an empty one is rejected by the server (400) and cannot be submitted from the form, and the token row and its set are written in one transaction. It does not stay non-empty for life, and the stronger wording this invariant used to carry — "a token without a scope is observable in no read" — was disproved on a live stack. Deleting a workspace narrows every token's basket and deliberately stops short of revoking the credential, which is not the purger's call to make, so a live token with an empty basket is reachable. It now answers 403 naming that cause, rather than the 400 that used to ask the caller to name one of zero workspaces.
Duplicates in workspaceIds are collapsed; the set in the response is what was actually granted.
A non-existent workspace in the set gives 400 rather than a token pointing nowhere; with no WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY bound, the check is skipped rather than failing the issue.
An archived workspace is a legitimate scope: existence is checked, not status.

An expiresAt in the past is rejected (400), and so is one that is not a valid ISO timestamp. An absent expiry means "never" — that includes an explicit null, which for a while was the one spelling that could not issue a non-expiring token: @IsOptional() skips the rest of the chain for null, the parser guarded on === undefined, and new Date(null) is the epoch, so the plainest way of saying "no expiry" came back as a date in the past. Fixed 2026-08-30; all four spellings are pinned together.
The status is derived rather than stored, and revocation beats expiry: a token with revoked_at is revoked whatever its expires_at.
Revocation is idempotent: a repeat DELETE answers 204, does not change revoked_at and does not add a log row. Only the call that actually killed a live token writes an event.
Issue and revoke are committed together with their event in one transaction: there is no token without an audit row and no audit row without a token.
An event payload never contains the secret or its hash — only the name, scope, workspaces, prefix and expiry.
The token management routes are reachable only with a session holding a tokens:* permission and never with a bearer token, whatever its scope.
The decision "may this caller perform this operation" is made by one AccessPolicy: the token's scope is expanded into an Actor and checked against the same @RequirePermissions as a session.
The permissions of the token creator's role never take part in an access decision; createdBy is used only as attribution on a write.
Unknown, revoked and expired tokens are indistinguishable from the outside — one 401.
A token cannot work in a workspace outside its set: a foreign X-Workspace-Id is 403, even if the token covers exactly one workspace.
The header is required exactly when the set is larger than one: with a single workspace it is unnecessary, with several its absence is 400 rather than a silent choice made on the caller's behalf.
A token with several workspaces appears in the list under each of them and exactly once (the filter is set membership, not a join).
last_used_at is updated no more than once every 60 seconds, never blocks the request and never fails it if the write errors.
The UI is fail-closed: without tokens:read the page makes not a single request; without tokens:create there are no issue buttons; without tokens:delete the whole actions column is gone.
A list load error and an empty list are different screen states; a workspace load error in the dialog is likewise separated from "there are no workspaces".
The page number lives in the URL, an invalid value collapses to the first page, and a page beyond the list is clamped to the last.
Revocation does not leave focus on <body>: it is moved to a live element if Radix's restoration lost it.
The hosts contain no domain logic: no guards, no tables, no API routes, no screens. Adding a capability never requires editing a file in packages/bootstrap.
Every onPluginInit runs before NestFactory.create, strictly in array order, each awaited.
A throw in onPluginInit aborts the start, is logged with the plugin's name and is rethrown to the caller.
trust proxy is applied before anything that reads req.ip, and only if a value was given.
The body ceiling is set explicitly and never inherited from express.json(); exceeding it is a 413 from the parser, before any controller or guard.
The global ValidationPipe always carries all three flags: whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted, transform.
The API documentation is generated after the prefix and the pipe are set and before listen.
The reference routes are registered on the HTTP adapter rather than in Nest's router: they are outside the global prefix, outside the guards and outside the ValidationPipe.
The JSON route is registered before the UI, so it wins the collision when it sits underneath it.
Both documentation routes ride on one flag: the JSON is unreachable exactly when the UI is. Switched off, setupApiDocs returns null and mounts nothing.
A throw in one plugin's decorate neither blocks the start nor cancels the other plugins' contributions.
Operation tags are set only on the eight HTTP method keys; nothing writes tags into a path item's parameters or $ref.
The SPA fallback never answers a path under the API prefix, under /reference, a non-GET/HEAD method, a path with a file extension, or a request that does not accept HTML.
A missing admin bundle is a warning, not a failed start: the API comes up without a UI.
Static serving is mounted last, after every controller and both reference routes.
enableShutdownHooks is called before listen; SIGTERM drains requests rather than tearing connections.
createServer returns the listening application — otherwise an embedding host and a test cannot close it.
migrations.dir is a function, evaluated only at migration time and never at load time.
Every plugin carrying migrations has its own bookkeeping table; plugin histories never intersect.
Migrations are applied in plugin-array order, with no transaction spanning two plugins; a failure names the plugin and how many are already committed.
Authentication schemes come only from ServerPlugin.docs; the host invents none.
Every slot contribution is wired before the first render, in one call, from an empty state — a second run does not double the items.
Slot.getItems() returns a copy: one consumer's changes are invisible to another.
The host neither defines nor reads a single slot.
Public routes are mounted as top-level siblings, private ones as children of exactly one pathless parent carrying the first layout found.
The * → / wildcard lives inside the private group, not beside it.
A second layout contributor and a duplicate path produce a console.warn naming the plugins involved; the host never picks a winner silently.
A missing mount element is an exception naming the id it looked for, not a type assertion and a failure inside React.
<html lang> and <html dir> are set before the render.
The error boundary sits above BrowserRouter (catching a router throw) and below Toaster in terms of coverage — toasts survive a tree crash.
The announcing live region is mounted and empty before the first navigation; the first page load is not announced.
Only a changed heading is announced; if nothing changes within 5 seconds, no announcement happens at all.
The announcer does not move focus — that is the arriving page's decision.
A missing translation is reported at most once per identifier and at warn level; when the locale matches the default it is not reported at all.
The admin host imports no authorization package at all: identity-admin is absent from its dependencies.
The server host does not depend on express directly; the request and response types are declared structurally.

One implementation for two worlds. The monorepo and any generated application apply migrations through the very same applyPluginMigrations; the Nx executors are thin adapters, not a second implementation.
migrate and studio never run against a stale dist/: both build the server first, then read the compiled config.
An empty or missing database URL is a refusal, not a fallback to libpq's local defaults.
Plugins migrate in exactly the order buildPlugins() returned them. The order is never rearranged, sorted, or derived from dependencies.
A plugin without a migrations descriptor is skipped; if there are no such plugins at all, no connection is opened.
Every plugin is tracked in its own history table (migrations.table), so plugins are versioned independently.

A migration failure names the plugin, the number already committed, the total, and points at the ordering as the likely cause; the original error is preserved in cause; plugins after the failing one are not attempted.
The connection pool is closed on both success and failure (finally).
No log contains credentials: the target is described as host:port/database, and an unparseable URL as (unparseable DATABASE_URL) rather than as a guess.

The credential for Drizzle Studio is never written to disk: the ephemeral config references process.env.DATABASE_URL, the URL is passed through the child process's environment, and the temporary folder is removed in finally.
Binding Studio to anything other than loopback prints a warning with the address before startup.
The build never bundles: plugin migrations must remain files inside their packages in node_modules.
tsc and vite are resolved from the application's node_modules and only through its manifest's bin field — not from the CLI's tree and not by guessing a subpath.
.env does not overwrite already-exported environment variables; a missing file is neither an error nor a warning.
.env is read once, before the command dispatcher, so that every spawned process inherits the values.
dev populates dist/ with a one-shot build before starting node --watch.
Shutting dev down — by any child exiting or by a signal — takes all the others with it, exactly once (the settling flag).
Termination by SIGINT/SIGTERM for dev, start and studio is a success, exit code 0.
Any exception that reaches the top is printed as a single message line without a stack trace, and the process exits with code 1.
generate never connects to a database: generation only compares the schema against a snapshot, which is why there are — and must be — no secrets in the drizzle configs.
The migration name reaches drizzle-kit as a single literal argv element, with no shell involved: a hostile name is merely a strange name.
The application layout is a convention (LAYOUT), not configuration: the CLI reads no settings file of its own.
The compiled config is read through require, not await import() — otherwise module.default turns out to be a wrapper rather than the config.
findProjectRoot walks up to the nearest package.json, so a command works from any subdirectory of the application.
Content types are declared in code only; no HTTP route creates, changes or deletes a type or a field.

The registry is built eagerly at startup: a duplicate name, an unresolvable relation target, an unpaired relationInverse and a GraphQL name collision abort the application's boot rather than the first request.
A type with i18n: true and no bound CONTENT_ENTRY_EXTENSION aborts startup (EntryExtensionBootCheck).
Every content row belongs to exactly one workspace, and every read, write and bulk operation ANDs workspace_id. An id from another workspace reads as a 404.

An unknown and an ungranted :typeName give the same 404 with the same text, and the grants are read before any registry decision — on all four surfaces (the session API, the public REST, GraphQL, the tools).
The reserved envelope columns (status, published_at, deleted_at, locale, locale_group_id) can neither be declared as a field nor set from a request body.
On a publishable type, required fields are nullable columns and the required check runs at publication against the stored row; on a non-publishable one they are NOT NULL and checked on every write.
Saving a publishable entry always yields status = draft while preserving published_at; only unpublish clears it.
Publication re-validates the stored row rather than the submitted values; a gate failure is a 422 { message, issues }, and the entry does not go live.
At any moment one entry has at most one version in published status: markPublished demotes the previous live one to superseded in the same transaction.
Version history is append-only: restoring yields a new version, publishing an earlier version creates no copy, and no version is ever rewritten or deleted.
Version numbers are monotonic and unique within one entry_id — allocated under an advisory lock on the entry and backstopped by a unique index.
The version, the row, its links, the write extensions' state and the domain event commit in one transaction or not at all.
entry.updated is not raised when no field value changed; a bulk write raises one event per actually changed row rather than per id passed.
Every row rewritten by any extension (a shared field, an audience) gets its own version, with deduplication — one save never gives one row two versions.
A public read serves published content only by default; ?status=draft|any requires content:update, and a guard checks it, not the query.
The CONTENT_READ_SCOPE fragments can only narrow a read; they are not applied to the admin UI's records list.
An unreachable relation target appears in neither items nor total: the restriction goes inside the window and inside the count(*).

A link does not cross locales when both sides are localized; the rule is applied by the writer (one assertSameLocale implementation reachable from all three write paths), not only by the admin UI's picker.
A group write takes its locale from the query string, never from body.locale — that field is for creation only.
A relations key that owns no writable link from this side is a 400: a delta is never lost silently.
A structurally malformed relation delta is a 400 at the DTO level rather than a 500 out of the query; the arrays and the map are size-bounded.
A malformed relation target uuid is a uniform 422 rather than a 500 from a Postgres cast error.
?fields= narrows values and the SQL projection, the envelope always comes back, an unknown name is a 400, and an empty parameter reads as “no preference”.
The filter picker physically cannot offer a path the API will reject: the list and the SQL schema come out of one buildEntryFilterSurface walk; a drift test pins it.
Every virtual filter field's subquery is scoped by the workspace passed in; on a name collision the first declarer wins, not the last.
The GraphQL schema is built per the workspace's grant set, so introspection cannot enumerate types the workspace was not granted; the cache TTL is a freshness knob, not a security boundary.
GraphQL mutation input fields have no defaultValue, otherwise merging by key presence would turn into overwriting every omitted field.
Both protocols reject the same input with the same message: the DTOs are validated in the GraphQL resolvers and in the agent tools alike.
No copilot tool writes to the database: all three write tools have effect: 'propose', and applying goes through the same EntryWriterService.create/.update as the HTTP routes.
The copilot's tools have no status parameter on any role; bulk publication and bulk deletion are absent from them too.
A change that reaches into other locales is disclosed in the proposal's summary and in target.fanout — against the patched values.
Grants are re-checked when a proposal is applied; “not granted” and “does not exist” give one message.
A saved view is a bookmark, not a grant: the payload is replayed with the reader's permissions, workspace and grants, so it cannot show more.

Someone else's view is neither edited nor deleted even by an administrator; setting a personal default is not restricted to the owner; visibility: 'workspace' requires views:share and is checked on every write.
A view's scope is resolved through the registry and the grants, answering with the same 404 — otherwise the endpoint would be a way around ContentGrantGuard.
The @orthacms/content-domain kernel has no dependencies; the entries/domain/ layer imports neither NestJS, nor Drizzle, nor class-validator, nor its own infrastructure (checked by grep).
Value validation and the publication gate exist in one copy — in the kernel; the admin UI does not mirror them, it localizes the stable English reason.
An editor without write permission is read-only throughout, not just in its buttons; runSave returns early, because a <form> submits on Enter in a text field.

A failed type catalogue gives an error state with a retry rather than empty navigation; a URL parameter outside the allowed range degrades rather than leaving the reader in an error card with no way out.
The copilot has no identity of its own: every run executes as the caller, and copilot_proposals.created_by is always a person.
The capability profile is recomputed on every run and re-checked on every tool call against freshly resolved grants. Nothing is cached across a conversation.
An observer is offered no tool with an effect other than read. That is a unit test over a pure function rather than an e2e hope.
No publish tool exists for any role (ADR-0005 §7).
The one point of call authorization is ToolRegistry.call, checking requires before dispatch; the offer filter is only a convenience on top of it.
The first declaration of a tool name wins; a later one goes into withheld with duplicate-name and cannot pass itself off as a native tool.
A propose/apply tool absent from the branch's allowed_tools parks the run before execution. Reads never ask.
allowed_tools is read per call rather than per run, and appended to in SQL.
Only a parked run's own user, in their workspace, may answer it or extend its deadline; everything else is the same 404 as “nothing is waiting”.
The waiting budget is per run rather than per call; an exhausted one refuses immediately without holding the connection.
Every broker exit — an answer, a timeout, an abort — clears the entry; no dangling promises remain.
The copilot_proposals row is written by the engine and before the apply; a binder that wrote directly would be a change with no receipt.
The apply goes through the owning plugin's ProposalApplier, which calls the ordinary use case with a person as the actor: the same validation, the same revision, the same activity row.
The status is flipped by a status = 'pending' predicate before the write, so the applier is unreachable twice for one row.
A failed apply reopens the row as pending with the message; pending means failure, and nobody retries automatically.
The audit row agrees with the outcome rather than with the dispatch: a failed apply gives ok = false.
A row is written for every attempt at a tool call — succeeded, failed, and refused by the user or by a timeout.
executeTool never throws: an unknown tool, a revoked permission, malformed arguments, a failed tool — all come back as tool errors, and the run carries on.
A repeated identical call (the name + the arguments with sorted keys) is rejected with an explanation, and the check runs after authorization.
Every tool result enters the model through fenceUntrusted; the closing delimiter cannot be forged from inside, and exceeding the size is replaced by an envelope that declares the truncation.
A run is bounded by three ceilings; the wall clock is checked before every tool call as well, and a call refused on a ceiling still returns a tool_result.
Exactly one done ends the stream; an abort ends the stream rather than throwing out of it; an aborted call reports zero spend. Verified by the conformance suite on all three adapters.
text-delta is forwarded through yield* as it arrives; collecting into an array and flushing afterwards would disable streaming invisibly.
The user's message is stored before the model call; attachments and skills are resolved before the conversation is touched.
The assistant's turn is stored even on a cancellation and a failure; the transcript is append-only and is not edited after the write.
An attachment shortfall and unresolvable skills report a count, never which id or name.
A run request carries skill names, never instruction text; an always skill is applied on the server regardless of what the client sent.
A skill has and can have no field narrowing or widening the tool set: a skill changes how, never what is allowed.
A code-defined skill wins a name collision; the CMS row is discarded, and the write routes refuse a colliding name up front (409).
Every repository method reachable from a route filters on both userId and workspaceId; “no such thing” and “not yours” give the same 404.
modelChoice is validated against ModelRegistry.catalogue() on write and cannot name a backend the operator did not configure.
PATCH /conversations/:id does not bump updatedAt, and the ownership predicate sits in the UPDATE itself.
A conversation cannot be deleted, only archived; the active and archived lists are disjoint. A skill can be deleted.
With enabled: false no controller at all is registered, while the shared ToolRegistry stays identical on both sides of the toggle.
CopilotPlugin refuses to construct with the copilot enabled and no providers, with a provider that has no models, with a non-positive maxOutputTokens, or with any non-positive ceiling.
A vendor SDK is imported by only provider-anthropic; copilot-domain has no dependencies block at all.
provider-fake is marked private and excluded from the release projects; no composition root registers it.
Attaching a file gives the copilot no new write path: the upload is an ordinary POST /api/media/assets under the user's own media:create.
Client-disconnect detection hangs on res, never on req.
The admin UI treats the copilot as switched off only on an explicit 404 from the model catalogue; a load, a 5xx, a 403 and a network failure all leave the surfaces in place.
Every publishable @orthacms/* package under packages/ is classified in features.ts exactly once: core, dev core, a capability's packages, or transitive. An unclassified package fails a test.
The classification holds no name absent from the disk (the one allowed exception is @orthacms/cli).
Every @orthacms/* dependency of a generated application is pinned to the scaffolder's exact version — no caret, no range, no latest.

No @orthacms/* version is written down in features.ts or in any template file — every one is stamped at render time from the scaffolder's own manifest. features.ts holds no version number at all; a template's own third-party dependency ranges are its business.
A rendered application contains not one __PLACEHOLDER__ token and not one ortha:if|ifnot|end directive.
package.json never passes through the conditional blocks: its dependency set is assembled in code.
An unclosed ortha:if and an unpaired ortha:end throw, naming the file, rather than returning a truncated file.
A nested block inside a discarded one stays discarded, whatever its own condition says.
Marker lines are always removed — both when a block is kept and when it is discarded.
REST cannot be switched off: lockedOf(PROTOCOLS) is added to any answer, --protocols none included; the picker's cursor does not land on a locked row and the space bar does not toggle it.
Exactly one storage adapter is installed and exactly one is constructed in MediaServerPlugin; exactly one type is assigned to the plugins.media.storage field.
Exactly one storage adapter is marked enabledByDefault && available.
Every optional capability (the copilot backends, all of SSO, the unlocked protocols) starts switched off.
copilot-server and copilot-admin are present in every application, and copilot-provider-fake in none: it is a private fixture, not a published package.
COPILOT_ENABLED=false and MCP_ENABLED=false are always written into .env, whatever was chosen.
A copilot backend and an SSO provider register only when their settings are present: an empty key means no item in the list rather than an item that fails on the first message.
The generated .env holds neither a SESSION_SECRET nor a TOKEN_SECRET: sessions and one-time tokens are opaque random values verified against a database row, and there is nothing to sign them with.
The administrator's password is generated rather than asked for, and exists in exactly two places: in .env (which is in .gitignore) and in one printed line.
An existing non-empty directory is never overwritten — the refusal comes before the first write.
The scaffolder never blocks on a prompt: no TTY or --yes means the defaults, and every question has a flag.
stdin is returned from raw mode to its original state on any outcome — an answer, a cancellation, an exception.
_gitignore arrives as .gitignore, and no *.tmpl file remains in the generated application.

The root tsconfig.json references exactly five projects, in the order server, the server's spec project (apps/server/tsconfig.spec.json), admin, server-e2e, admin-e2e. The server contributes two because the build project excludes the specs, so without a project of their own nothing typechecks them.
apps/server/tsconfig.json excludes **/*.spec.ts, or the tests end up in dist/server.
styles.css contains the exact line @source "../../../node_modules/@orthacms"; and contains no @source with a glob inside a node_modules path.
The Vite config is named vite.config.mts, not .ts.
DatabasePlugin is first in the server list; identity precedes workspaces among the migrating plugins; McpPlugin, where present, is last.
In the admin UI exactly one plugin supplies a layout, and it is shell; identity comes first.
The expected plugin list in the generated application's plugins.spec.ts matches the actual one for any combination of capabilities.
A template file outside the text-extension list is copied byte for byte, with no substitutions.
The templates/ directory is excluded from Nx inference, the TypeScript build, linting and formatting — in all four places at once.
The package has zero runtime dependencies.
There is exactly one pool and one Drizzle client per process. initDatabase is idempotent: a repeat call does not open a second pool, it increments the holder counter.
getDatabase() and getPool() before initDatabase throw with an intelligible message rather than returning undefined.

The pool is always opened with explicit max and connectionTimeoutMillis; the latter is strictly greater than zero. Exhausting the pool must produce an error on one request, not an unbounded wait for all of them.
The pool is closed by the last holder to leave. An application shutting down while a neighbour in the same process is alive does not take the database away from it.
closeDatabase clears the memo before ending the pool: afterwards initDatabase opens a genuinely new pool rather than handing out an ended one.
The shutdown hook never lets an exception out — the error is only logged and the rest of the shutdown runs.
A nested UnitOfWork.run joins the outer transaction and never opens a new one.
uow.current() outside a run returns the base connection and does not throw — reading outside a unit of work is legitimate.
OutboxWriter.append outside a UnitOfWork.run throws. An event cannot be written on a separate connection.
An event commits if and only if the state change that raised it commits. A rollback takes the events with it.
append with an empty array is a silent no-op: no query and no error.
Repeating one eventId within a unit of work fails the whole unit of work — the eventId is the outbox row's primary key.
A post-commit drain failure never rolls back the state change — the exception is swallowed and the poll picks the event up.
A row is stamped dispatched_at only after every matching subscriber has finished without throwing.
One subscriber's failure increments attempts and sets next_attempt_at, leaving the row undelivered; the batch's other rows are delivered normally.
A row with attempts ≥ 15 no longer enters the selection — a full batch of “poisoned” rows cannot block the head of the queue.
nextAttemptAfter(n, now) > now for every n; the delay doubles from 1 second and plateaus at 5 minutes.
Within a process, no more than one drain runs at a time, plus at most one deferred. The pool cannot be exhausted by drains.
Drains in different processes take disjoint rows and do not block each other (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).
onModuleDestroy waits out the in-flight drain and throws no exception; the wait is bounded by one batch.
An event with no subscribers at all is marked delivered immediately, with attempts = 0.
attachActor does not mutate the input events, puts the actor under the actor key and overwrites an actor placed there by the publisher.
The package owns exactly one table. A second one appearing is a change of architectural decision, not a routine edit.
There is no domain/ module in this package and none should appear: this is infrastructure.
No file in src/ imports through the @/ alias — only through relative paths.
Everything meant for a consumer is exported from src/index.ts; the package hands out no public subpaths other than ./styles.css and ./package.json.
No component contains a literal colour: only semantic Tailwind utilities expanding into var(--color-*).
Every light-palette token has a counterpart in .dark — either overridden or deliberately inherited (the panel's chrome and the navigation accents).
A caller's className prop always beats the component's base classes: cn puts it last and tailwind-merge gives a conflict to the last one.
The package contains neither react-intl nor a translation catalogue; every visible string either arrives as a prop or has an English default overridable through DesignSystemLabelsProvider.
DesignSystemLabelsProvider takes a Partial: a missing key keeps its English default, so adding a key does not break an existing consumer.
A prop at the call site (closeLabel, label) always beats the value from the labels context.
Spinner and Skeleton are decorative and announce nothing themselves; busyness is announced only by a named role="status" (SkeletonRegion, AppLoader, WizardPageSkeleton).
There is exactly one live region per loading surface; two mounted at once is a defect.
FieldError returns null when there are no messages; an empty role="alert" is never opened.
invalid in InputField governs only the control's marking and never suppresses the error message.
A control's aria-describedby is assembled from the hint, the error and the value the caller passed — none of the three is lost.
AlertTitle, CardTitle and EmptyTitle are not headings by default; the rank is set by the page through asChild.
Alert writes aria-labelledby only after AlertTitle has actually mounted.
The Table wrapper takes a tab stop only on actual overflow; the group role and the name are set exclusively together.
SidebarInset's scrollport is focusable and draws a visible ring when it receives focus; the ring is inset, because the parent clips overflow.

No nameable container in the library adds a second landmark: group is used, not region. The only landmarks the library creates are the <main> of SidebarInset/AppLoader, the complementary of a named panel, and the <nav> of the breadcrumbs, the link tabs and the pagination.
A collapsed offcanvas panel is marked inert: its controls are outside the tab order and outside the accessibility tree.
Ctrl/⌘+B is not intercepted when focus is in a text input, a textarea, a select or inside a contenteditable.
useIsMobile returns the right value on the first render frame, not after an effect.
The library's single layout breakpoint is 768px; 768 inclusive counts as desktop.
Every access to localStorage, document.cookie and matchMedia is wrapped in an environment check and a try/catch; a storage failure loses only the persistence of the preference.
The theme is applied to the document in two ways at once: the dark class on <html> and style.colorScheme — so the browser repaints its own furniture too.
useAppearance outside an AppearanceProvider does not throw: it returns the defaults and a no-op setter.
useSidebar outside a SidebarProvider throws; for an optional dependency there is useOptionalSidebar.
TopBar inside an inset renders only through a portal into the bar; while the bar's host is null the bar is not drawn at all, so it does not flash in the page flow.
Clicking a toast's body dismisses that toast; clicks on the close button, the action/cancel buttons and links inside the toast are not intercepted.
Toasts are positioned in the bottom right corner, and that is decided in Toaster rather than at the call site: copilot-admin relies on it when suppressing a toast while the dock is open.

Every non-operable animation is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — with one deliberate exception, the loading spinner, which is stripped of movement rather than stopped: opacity only, no transform, a cycle no faster than 1 s. A stopped indeterminate loader is indistinguishable from a hung request, and WCAG 2.3.3 is about non-essential motion, not about withholding essential feedback.
The wizard step's animation changes only the transform; opacity stays at 1, so the content is visible even with animation clocks stopped.
Under forced-colors: active, every :focus-visible has a real outline; forced-color-adjust: none is used nowhere.
No state is carried by colour alone: a selected segment and an active panel item additionally thicken the font, and status dots are always accompanied by text.
White text is never placed on bg-brand; there is a separate brand-text token for link orange.
A wizard step list item's key is its position, not its caption: the caption belongs to the consumer and may repeat.
A row in MultiSelect is identified by its value, with the caption added as keywords — otherwise two options with the same caption merge into one.
The package exports nothing server-side and has no routes, no module, no tables and no permission keys.
The only peer dependencies are react and react-dom at ^19; everything else is an ordinary dependency, so a consumer has nothing extra to install.

Exactly one default locale. Checked at plugin construction (LocaleSet.create: defaults.length !== 1 → InvalidLocaleSetError). Consequence: LocaleSet.default() is a total function, and no other code handles “what if there is no default”.
The locale set is non-empty and the slugs are unique. An empty array and a duplicate slug fail in the same place, before startup, before the first request.
A locale slug is a BCP-47 tag in lowercase form. /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, no longer than 35. Nothing in the code upper-cases the region — the value is dropped into lang verbatim.
The writing direction is always present on the wire. dir is optional in the config, but Locale.dir is always resolved (declared or inferred). A consumer sets dir unconditionally rather than guessing.

An unknown slug is a 400, never a substitution of the default. The single gate is LocalePolicy.resolve, wrapped by LocaleRegistryService.resolve. The rule is mirrored on the client: findLocale returns undefined on a miss.
The absence of ?locale= means the default locale. Which is why the default locale is written as a clean URL in the admin UI (toLocaleListParam) — the two spellings cannot diverge.
The fallback chain is no longer than two. Only [requested] or [requested, default], and only with ?localeFallback=default. There is no hierarchical fallback (pt-br → pt → en).

Every port hook is a no-op on a non-localized type. All six methods open with a type.i18n check. Binding the extension cannot change an unrelated type's behaviour — that is a requirement of the port's contract, not a courtesy.

One row per (group, locale) pair. The arbiter is the database's unique index (partial on paranoid types, WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), not a check in code. A duplicate is always a 409, never a corrupted group.

A localeGroupId on creation must name an existing group in this workspace — otherwise a 404. A typo cannot spawn a stray one-row group. The TOCTOU window is harmless: the row stays valid, and duplicates are caught by the index anyway.

An ordinary creation starts its own group. The id comes from the column's default (gen_random_uuid()) rather than from code — so “start a new group” and “join an existing one” differ by the presence of one argument.
The group lock is taken before any row lock. beforeWrite is the transaction's first statement. Ordering siblings by id remains, but as determinism rather than as deadlock protection.

A save with nothing to propagate takes no sibling locks. The “are there shared columns or a synchronized relation” check runs before the read. Both inputs are free: the columns come from the save's own value bag, and a relation's synchronizability is a property of the schema.
A sibling where everything matches is not rewritten. No history row, no demotion, no updatedAt. The comparison uses IS DISTINCT FROM, with every value bound by its own column's encoder.

A rewritten published sibling goes to draft, keeping published_at. It reads as Modified, not as a draft that was never published. Publishing any locale remains per-row; this rule merely stops one locale from going live on someone else's save.

A sibling that was published must remain valid. Re-validation reads the pre-write statuses taken with SELECT … FOR UPDATE; a failure is a 422 and a rollback of the whole save. Drafts need no validation — the same rule as when saving a draft directly.
An unresolvable mirrored relation is nulled, not left. A left value would point at the translation of the previous entry — silently wrong data is worse than an empty field.

A mirrored link to an untranslated target is simply not set and does not fail the save. An English save must not fail because the German tag does not exist yet. That is equivalentIdsByLocale's job — the lenient twin of resolveLocaleGroups, which throws a 422 (right for an explicit API call, wrong for implicit synchronization).

Creation pulls relations inward rather than pushing them outward. The donor is picked deterministically: the default locale's row, otherwise the lexicographically first. The derived columns are appended to row in place, because the snapshot for version 1 is taken after the call.

Revisions are written by content, not by i18n. afterUpdate returns the rewritten rows and the pipeline appends a version for each in the same transaction. Numbering is serialized by an advisory lock; a second writer handing out numbers around it is a way to produce duplicate versions.

hasLocale accepts only eq and in. ne/nin negate inside the EXISTS and answer a different question. The refusal is a 400 naming the field. The admin drawer mirrors the same restriction so as not to offer a rule the API will reject.
missingLocale in [a, b] means “all of the listed ones are missing”. It is a notExists over the union. “At least one is missing” is expressed as an or of missingLocale eq rules.

The virtual filters and coverage are bounded by the same configured set. The extension's groupScope and the coverage query's configuredScope. Without this the two views of one entry would diverge: localeCount would drift above the configured total.
Coverage's unit is an entry, not a row. count(distinct locale_group_id) everywhere. The per-type rows sum to the envelope's totals — a dedicated server-e2e test checks this.
With one configured locale, notLocalized is forced to 0. Otherwise every entry would report itself as both fully localized and not localized at all.

The summary response's keys are exactly the request's keys. Every requested id is seeded with [] and the rows are workspace-scoped: another workspace's group and a non-existent id are indistinguishable.

The agent's tools re-check the type grants, the HTTP path does not. A type name from the model is steerable by the content it read; a type name from the UI has already passed a workspace-scoped controller.

A propose tool accepts localized fields only, and the applier must mix in the source's shared values, read at apply time. Otherwise coerceValues stamps the shared fields as null, and a group of drafts is silently nulled in every language.
The batch applier writes sequentially and stops at the first error, naming how many landed. A proposal has one row and one status — there is no per-item verdict.
An error is not an emptiness. The admin's three reads (useLocales, useEntryLocales, useLocaleSummaries) must distinguish “no data” from “couldn't ask”, and every surface draws that as its own state.
Cross-locale relations are forbidden. The picker's candidates are scoped strictly by the active locale, with no fallback. Correspondingly, the applier does not copy the source's per-locale relations.
The plugin owns no table and ships no migration. The absence of a drizzle.config.ts is part of the package's contract, not an oversight.
Every route is closed by default: AuthGuard is registered as an APP_GUARD, and being public is only ever explicit, through @Public().
Only an account with status active gets a session; the status check is repeated on every request, not only at sign-in.
Every reason for a failed sign-in is indistinguishable — in the response and in timing alike.
Every reason for an invalid one-time token renders as one bare 404 with no body.
A one-time token activates an account or changes a password exactly once, even under concurrent requests.
Consuming a reset revokes all of the account's sessions and issues no new one.
Signing out revokes only the presented session and always succeeds (idempotency).
Changing a password revokes the account's live sessions, keeping the caller's own session when one is named.
Not one secret is stored in plaintext: passwords are bcrypt(12); session, link, API and SSO-attempt tokens are SHA-256.
An API token's secret is returned exactly once, at issue time, and never reaches an event, a log or a repeat response.
A password is accepted at ≥ 12 characters and ≤ 72 UTF-8 bytes; exceeding the ceiling is a refusal, not silent truncation.
Email is unique case-insensitively at the database level.
System roles cannot be deleted (the SQL condition is_system = false), and role seeding is idempotent and safe when several instances start at once.
The admin role holds the full permission set by enumeration; there are no wildcard permissions in the system.
The decision "may this actor perform this action" is made by a single implementation — AccessPolicy; both the session guard and the content API's bearer guard delegate to it.
Listing and revoking somebody else's sessions requires users:update, not users:read.
The current flag in the session list is true only for the caller's own session.
An API token's scope is a non-empty workspace set; a non-existent id gives 400 rather than a token issued "into nowhere".
The API-token management routes are reachable only with an administrator's session and never with a bearer token.
Any SSO failure is one and the same redirect to ?error=sso; no distinguishable reason leaves the system.
An SSO attempt is consumed before the token exchange, and the exchange happens outside the transaction.
A first SSO sign-in claims an existing account only with emailVerified: true; pending and disabled are rejected exactly as on the password path.
Role mapping never demotes an account that already holds the admin role; an unknown role key is logged and ignored.
JIT creation is impossible without a non-empty domain list; the match is exact on the domain, not on a suffix.
Back-channel logout is idempotent, always carries cache-control: no-store, and answers 404 for a provider that cannot verify a logout token.
The application refuses to start with SSO providers registered and cookieSameSite: 'strict'.
The identity-domain package has no dependencies; the domain/ layer in identity-server imports neither NestJS, nor Drizzle, nor class-validator.
In the admin UI, a "who am I" probe failing for any reason other than 401 gives the unavailable state rather than a redirect to sign-in.
useHasPermission is fail-closed: false in every state except authenticated.
A change of identity in a tab clears the whole query cache except the auth namespace.
The package imports not one feature package. Its dependencies are only bootstrap-admin, design-system, utils-admin, workspaces-admin, identity-admin.
The package contributes not one item into INSIGHTS_WIDGET_SLOT.
No widget disappears silently: a widget with an unregistered section ends up in the trailing band marked data-section-fallback="true".
A band left with no visible widget is not rendered at all — heading included.
Sections are merged by id and the last contribution wins — field by field and only for the fields actually given; the band's position stays the first one.
Widget and section sorting is stable: an equal order across two plugins preserves registration order rather than leaving it to object traversal.
An item with no order gets DEFAULT_INSIGHTS_ORDER = 100, that is, it lands after the built-in 10/20/30/40 rather than in the middle.
A widget whose permission the user lacks is excluded from the layout; the permission filter applies to the orphans in the fallback band too.
The permission is checked twice: on the slot item, before the band heading is rendered, and in the data hook, through enabled.
WidgetCard resolves exactly one of the four branches; isError outranks isEmpty.
On failure StatWidget never prints a number: an em dash plus hidden "Unavailable" text.
The corner chip and the summary caption under the body are shown only when there is data.
A throw inside one widget does not unmount its neighbours: each is wrapped in its own WidgetBoundary.
Changing the range clears the failure recorded by the boundary (resetKey = range), so a crash is not permanent.
Every widget opens its own request; the page itself makes not a single network request.
Every Insights request sets retry: 1 rather than the default three.
Every widget's cache key contains the workspace id; period-dependent ones also contain days. The workspace reaches the server only in a header, which is not sent on a cache hit.
The range's source of truth is the URL. The default value is not written into the URL; an unknown value falls back to the default; the write uses replace and merges with the existing parameters.
useInsightsRange outside its provider returns the default and an empty setRange rather than throwing.
An unknown size value gives the md width rather than one column out of twelve; the check is Object.hasOwn, not a plain key read.
All width and palette classes are written as whole literals: Tailwind will not emit an interpolated class name, and the bars would render transparent.
A zero BarRows segment is not drawn but is named in the track's aria-label.
No caption for the q0…q5 ladder describes colour ("darker", "lighter") — only magnitude: the ladder's direction flips between themes.
The heading structure has no gaps: h1 for the page, h2 for a section band, h3 for a card (the error boundary's placeholder included).
The package owns no database table, has no server half, and ships no migrations.
Authentication precedes the protocol. An unauthenticated caller cannot move the JSON-RPC state machine at all, initialize included. The answer is an ordinary HTTP 401, not a JSON-RPC error.
The verb check follows authentication. An unauthenticated GET is a 401, not a 405: the answer about the verb is unreachable without credentials.
A session cookie is not a credential for this endpoint — never, in any mode.
An unknown, a revoked and an expired token are indistinguishable — one flat 401 with no hint which of the three it was.
A bearer value contains no internal whitespace. The pieces after the scheme are not glued together: an invented token would report itself as “wrong secret” instead of “malformed header”.

The workspace is always resolved before dispatch and always belongs to the token's basket. The header wins over the query; both spellings pass the same check. More than one named workspace is a 400, not a silent pick.
An actor's permissions are derived from the token's scope alone. The role of the human who minted it is never consulted — revoking the token is always sufficient, whoever issued it.
ToolRegistry.call is the only authorization boundary. visibleTo only hides; a client is free to name a name it was never shown. A handler does not check its own gate.
The surface narrowing applies both to the list and to a call. A ['copilot'] tool is neither visible nor callable here, however broad the token.
Authorization precedes argument validation. Someone who may not do this learns nothing about the arguments, and the answer is the same whatever they send.

The surface in the context is stamped by the registry, not by the caller. So a handler sees, by construction, the surface the tool was authorized against. It may be used for presentation only, never for authority.
A tools/call refusal is a result with isError, not a JSON-RPC error. A resources/* refusal is the reverse. Both halves go through toToolError, so the flattened error shape is the same.
An unexpected exception is opaque on both paths — 500 / internal_error and the text “see the logs”. A raw driver message never reaches the wire.
A result is returned in both spellings — as a text block and as structuredContent. A non-object is wrapped in { value }, not dropped.

Every exchange is bounded by three ceilings: the request body, the time of one call, the size of one result. Exceeding the time or the size is returned in a form the model can read (504/timeout, 413/result_too_large).
The deadline bounds the caller's wait, not the work. A tool that ignores the signal runs to completion. The caller gets an answer either way.
The transport and the protocol server live exactly one exchange and are closed on close. No session identifiers are issued or checked; an Mcp-Session-Id that is sent is ignored.
The tool list is a function of the caller. A read token and a full token get different lists from one and the same deployment.

No content rule is rewritten here. The handlers call the same resolveGrantedType, PublicEntriesQuery, PublicEntryWritesService the HTTP controllers do, and validate with the real DTOs under the host's ValidationPipe options.
The switch removes only the controller. The registry is bound and populated with MCP_ENABLED=false, because the copilot consumes the same registry. Symmetrically for COPILOT_ENABLED.
The plugin owns no table and no migration. No migrations descriptor is declared.

A broken catalogue does not survive to the first caller. A duplicate name, an invalid name, an empty surfaces, a non-existent permission, a malformed inputSchema — all of them abort app.init(), and every problem is reported at once.

Reading a resource is not a way around the grant gate. An ungranted type 404s on resources/read exactly as it does on a tool call; a resource's requires is checked before the provider is asked for any bytes.
Reading returns only published content by default. Only an actor with content:update can widen it to drafts.
Bytes never live in the database: an asset's row holds only a storage_key + storage_provider.
Exactly one storage provider runs in a deployment, passed as one object; there is no registry, no resolver and no defaultProvider.
provider.id is a fact about the adapter itself, written into every row; the application compares it on reads, deletions and purges rather than looking a backend up by name.
Startup aborts if media_asset holds rows from another provider; the message names it and the row count. A missing table is not a refusal.

capabilities.directUrl: true cannot be declared without a directUrl() implementation, and directServe: 'signed-url' cannot be set on a provider that does not sign. Both checks happen when the application is assembled.
put is all-or-nothing: a rejected call leaves no blob behind and hands out no key.
get rejects before opening a stream, and with an ObjectNotFoundError specifically, when the key is missing; remove is idempotent.
Every port method rejects a promise rather than throwing synchronously — a synchronous throw bypasses the try that frees the blobs.
A derivative can never overwrite an original: it is written into the reserved variants/ key space through PutObject.isVariant.
Derivative generation is best-effort: a source the processor cannot decode yields zero derivatives and never fails the upload.
A failed upload (a storage failure or a transaction rollback) frees every written blob, derivatives included.
Deletion frees blobs after the commit, over Asset.storageKeys — the original and every derivative; a rolled-back deletion destroys no bytes.
Uploading, moving and creating a subfolder take a FOR SHARE on the target folder and are therefore serialised against its cascading deletion.
A folder-deletion cascade filters by workspace in both branches of the recursive CTE, locks the subtree FOR UPDATE, returns the deepest first, and repeats the walk until it stabilises.
Every route is gated on a permission by the PERMISSIONS.MEDIA_* constant; state-changing session routes additionally carry OriginGuard.
Every route but GET /media/assets/:id/raw carries WorkspaceGuard; that one derives the scope from the asset's row and requires membership of the owning workspace.
A non-existent asset, another workspace, a missing membership and a blob missing from storage all give the same 404; the storage key never reaches the response body.
A key that resolves outside the storage root stays a 500: that is corrupted data, not the caller's error.
Both raw routes always set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and a capability-free CSP; inline is granted only to allowlisted types, and SVG is not among them.
The direct-serve redirect happens after authorization, carries a pinned type and disposition, and is accompanied by Cache-Control: private, no-store.
The upload ceiling is inclusive: exactly maxUploadBytes is accepted, one byte more is a 413. No route gives FileInterceptor local limits.
A filename is a leaf: /, \, control characters, an empty name and one longer than 255 are rejected by FileName, not silently cleaned.
?variant= is resolved through Object.hasOwn; a missing derivative is not an error but a fallback to the original.
An unparseable folderId and an unknown kind give a 400 from the query itself rather than a 500 from the driver; % and _ in a search match themselves.
Alt text is normalised identically on every path (trimmed, empty → null), so a space is never counted as coverage.
The token half can only upload and read bytes; media:update and media:delete are granted to no token scope.
A token upload is attributed to the user who issued the token; their role is not checked in the process — the decision was already made by the token's scope.
An asset in a different workspace inside the token's basket is also a 404, otherwise X-Workspace-Id would be advisory.
Registration with the tool registry and with the workspace purge registry is @Optional(): media comes up without the copilot, without MCP and without the workspaces plugin.
The three reading tools are visible to both surfaces and the two “proposals” to the copilot only; downloadPath is the only surface-dependent field, and it is presentation only.
media_asset_read is bounded by a MIME allowlist and a 256 KB ceiling applied during the read; a decoding error is fatal, except for a truncated tail.
media_propose_file takes a format from a closed enumeration, rejects a path in the name and is bounded to 1 MB; the applier calls the same UploadAssetUseCase the HTTP route does.
The domain/ layer imports neither @nestjs/* nor drizzle-orm nor class-validator nor infrastructure/.

A provider depends only on @orthacms/media-domain — the port's types, plus ObjectNotFoundError, which is a value — and its own vendor SDK. The port package declares no dependencies of any kind, so no adapter reaches NestJS, Drizzle or Express by any route: not in its manifest, not in its imports, and not transitively.
Deleting a workspace deletes the media rows and frees their blobs — without per-item domain events, with one delete per table.
In the admin UI, the absence of media:read starts no queries at all; a read failure gives an error state of its own with a retry rather than an empty state.
Changing page, search, filter or sort clears the selection; the page is pulled back into range when the result shrank.
A file picked on an entry's media field is not uploaded until the entry is saved; a failed upload aborts the whole save, and files that already uploaded are not uploaded a second time on retry.
A file inserted into an article's body is uploaded immediately — a body holds a URL, and a URL does not exist without bytes.
The admin UI's cache keys always contain the workspaceId.
The inference glob is exactly **/{drizzle.config.ts,ortha.config.ts,package.json}; not one target of this package is written onto a project by hand.
A project with a drizzle.config.ts gets db:generate and does not get db:migrate or db:studio.
A project with an ortha.config.ts gets db:migrate and db:studio — both uncacheable.
db:generate is uncacheable and declares neither inputs nor outputs against which it could be cached.
db:generate opens no database connection and requires no secret at all.
db:migrate and db:studio refuse to run with an empty database URL and never fall through to libpq's local defaults.
The URL check in db:migrate happens before the plugin list is built: nothing is opened and nothing is applied.
Migrations are applied strictly in the order buildPlugins() returned, each plugin under its own journal table.
A migration failure names the plugin and the number of plugins already committed, and points at the order as a likely cause; the pool is closed either way.
The database URL is never written to disk: Studio receives it through the child process's env, and the ephemeral config references process.env.DATABASE_URL.
The ephemeral config's temporary directory is removed in finally on any outcome.
--port=0 for Studio is a refusal, not a silent shrug.
Any --host other than loopback prints a warning about the missing authentication before Studio starts.
Stopping Studio with SIGINT/SIGTERM is a target success, not a failure.
build, pack and nx-release-publish are inferred only for a package under packages/ with a name in its manifest and a tsconfig.lib.json beside it.
A package.json that will not parse yields zero targets, not a failed graph computation.
A package with private: true gets only build.

nx-release-publish always points packageRoot at dist/pack/<projectRoot> rather than the project root; the executor is declared both in the inference and in targetDefaults, and the two declarations agree.
pack is uncacheable: it reads dist, which is not among its declared inputs.
Publishes are serialised behind a file lock; at any moment at most one package in the workspace is publishing.
The lock is held through the pause as well, and is released only by its owner (a matching pid).
A live holder refreshes the lock with a heartbeat; staleAfter bounds silence, not the duration of the work.
A dead holder's lock (ESRCH) is taken immediately, without waiting out staleAfter; an unreadable or corrupt one is treated as alive.
Before every publish the registry is probed with a single GET; any failure of that probe collapses to unknown and never becomes a cause of a failed publish.
An already-published version is skipped without a single write to the registry; an EPUBLISHCONFLICT that slips through is also read as success.
A 429 on a version bump is retried; a 429 on creating a name is terminal and gets exactly one attempt.
The first blocked creation trips the safety catch, and the remaining new names in that run drop out without spending a single request.
An error that is not the registry's (a broken manifest, a missing entry point, a rejected token) fails on the first attempt.
A dry run neither probes the registry nor waits out the pause.
Precedence for the numeric settings: environment → target option → default; 0 from the environment is accepted as a value.
The @orthacms/nx package stays private and is excluded from the release by an explicit !@orthacms/nx.

The database executors contain no implementation of their own: db:generate, db:migrate and db:studio call @orthacms/cli functions, and that is the single implementation for the monorepo and for a generated application.
The host's TypeScript is loaded through createTsJiti with legacy decorators; both executors use the same loader.
The package stays CommonJS: require/__dirname/__filename, never import.meta.
The payload on the wire is always well-formed. Incomplete rules and emptied groups drop out during serialisation. The user is entitled to hold a draft on screen; the server is not entitled to see it.

The client never writes a bare operator string. Every leaf goes through UI_TO_WIRE or through an explicit branch of the serialiser. An operator added to OP with no table entry and no branch must throw rather than travel silently.
A rule always has a field. The model knows no “rule without a field” state, which is why the field cell has no destructive “clear” — it simply reopens.

An unknown field is not substituted. RuleRow resolves the field by id without falling back to fields[0]. Substituting someone else's field would drive the operator list and the validation by the wrong type while the rule still carries the old path: the row would look valid, and the Apply gate (which also resolves by id) would silently refuse the commit.

Changing the field resets both the operator and the value. Otherwise the rule is left with an operator legal for the previous type — and gets a 400 on the wire. Changing the operator likewise re-seeds the value by its shape (defaultValueForOp), otherwise composite operators get an '' and break the controls with a controlled → uncontrolled transition.

The default operator comes from opsForField, not from OPS_FOR_TYPE. The order a field declares is its default. Seeding from the type drove “Add rule” and the operator picker off two different dictionaries.

A declared operator list narrows but does not widen. It is filtered by what the type permits; a narrowing that matched nothing falls back to the type's full set — a picker with zero options is worse than a wrong order.

Every dictionary is read through Object.hasOwn. OPS_FOR_TYPE, UI_TO_WIRE, WIRE_TO_UI, MS_PER_UNIT, and the server's OPERATORS_BY_TYPE. These are ordinary object literals, and the key arrives from a public URL or from a schema built at runtime: WIRE_TO_UI['constructor'] would return Object, and the ?? null would never fire.

The serialiser is total. No value a user can type may throw during render: the preview serialises the live draft on every keystroke. Hence the clamping of within_last to a representable instant and the fallback of an unknown unit to days.
The deserialiser does not throw. Corrupt JSON, an unknown operator, a junk value — each yields null or a discarded rule. A user is capable of hand-editing ?filter=, and the page must survive it.
Every group owns its combinator. There is no global “AND/OR mode”; the root's switch and each subgroup's are independent, and every mutation is addressed by a node's id rather than by position.
React keys are never serialised. FilterGroup.id and FilterRule.id are client-side; they are regenerated when the URL is parsed.
An empty tree is null, not an empty group. treeToJsonFilter returns null and the consumer removes the parameter from the URL. Sending {and:[]} would get a FILTER_INVALID_NODE.
The draft is synced with the applied value on every opening. For the drawer and the panel alike. Closing without Apply discards the edits and clears the previous attempt's error state.

The Apply gate lets through no invalid rule, and in the absence of field definitions refuses all of them. That is why the fields' loading and error states are part of the panel's contract rather than polish: an empty picker reads as a dead button.
A broken rule always announces itself; an unfinished one does so after Apply. unknown_field and operator_not_allowed ignore showErrors: the user did not type them and has nothing to finish.
A filter the builder refuses to draw is one it does not send. The operator's legality is checked before every value check.
Focus after deleting a node stays inside the builder. The target is captured before the unmount and set in a requestAnimationFrame after it.

The picker's list is a valid listbox. Every navigable row is an option (the relation row too, with an aria-expanded instead of a value), headings are presentation, focus stays on the search box, and aria-activedescendant is live.

Inside a scroll-locking container, popovers portal into it. The portalContainer is published through context and must be read both by the field picker and by an injected relation editor, otherwise their lists do not scroll with the wheel.
relativeDates is passed if and only if the filter is stored. A link gets a frozen cut-off, a stored rule a sliding window. An error in either direction is silent and looks normal.
Until an audience is created, the plugin is inert: configured === false, the read scope returns undefined, no fragment is added, and a public read is byte for byte what it was before installation.
An entry with no entry_access row is read by everyone — that is what COALESCE(…, true) provides.
An empty allow list means “everyone”, not “nobody”.
A deny wins: a reader who falls into even one deny audience does not read the entry — however many allows they satisfy.
An anonymous reader (an empty tag set) sees exactly the entries with an empty allow, and there is no dedicated code branch for them.
The SQL predicate is canRead line for line: deny first, then the empty-allow case, then the intersection.
A restricted entry is absent from both items and total — across all three protocols and on every relation traversal.
Every && binds its list through uuidArray — as one sql.param, never by inlining the array into a template.
canRead never consults isOfferedIn: where an audience is offered is an editor's question, not a reader's.
An empty workspace_ids means “every workspace”, not “none” — in the schema, in the directory and in the “Offered in” control alike.
Narrowing an audience's scope does not revoke it from entries that already name it; validate exempts from the scope check every id the entry (or its locale group) already holds.
Deleting an audience sweeps it out of both sides of every entry in one transaction, and an entry left with two empty lists loses its row.
Two empty lists delete the row rather than being stored as a row of empty arrays.
An access write is a full replacement of both lists, not a merge.

Every write path checks that the entry id names a row of this workspace's content before writing anything, and answers a foreign id with the same 404 an id that exists nowhere gets. Added after the QA pass — see section 17.
Neither list may name more than 200 audiences, on every write path including the entry save's extensions bag. Added after the QA pass — see section 17.
Access is written across the entry's whole locale group, soft-deleted siblings included; the group is resolved from content's own locale_group_id column, with no dependency on @orthacms/i18n-server.
A write arriving in the extensions bag runs on the save's own transaction — never on a connection of the plugin's own.
Changing audiences requires segments:manage, checked in the extension; a request asking for exactly what is already saved changes nothing and needs no authority.
An actor that could not be identified (PrincipalStore.current() returned undefined) gets a 403, not a pass.
capture runs on every snapshot, not only on saves that touched access; for an unrestricted entry it returns undefined.
ACCESS_EXTENSION_KEY = 'access' is stable forever; restoring a version that did not name the key leaves the access untouched.
A restore that would change the audiences requires segments:manage; a restore matching the group's current state does not.
Every row of the locale group rewritten by apply gets a revision; the ids are deduplicated against the rows i18n reported.
Creating a translation inherits the group's audiences without a permission check and without a workspace-scope check, and only while the new row's access is still open.
withState and withStates always remove before they add: an audience never ends up in both lists at once.
