sameAccess is order-insensitive — a reordered list is not a pending change, in the staging or on the write path.
An empty staging (draft === null) does not send the access key at all, and the server leaves the audiences alone.
The tab's bulk action acts on the ids from the list response (every match), not on the rows on screen; past MATCHED_IDS_CAP the controls are disabled with an explanation.
Decisions on audiences absent from the current list are preserved and counted rather than discarded.
An entry's access cache key carries the workspace and the row's updatedAt; settle seeds the saved row and invalidates all the others.
The chip by the entry's title renders nothing while the workspace has no audiences.
Agent and public access reads answer from entry_access, not through a reader-scoped public entry read.
content_access_set exists on MCP only; the copilot gets content_propose_access with effect: 'propose' in its place, and both require segments:manage.
There is neither a public route nor an agent tool over the audience directory — under any token scope.
An accepted proposal's applier re-checks the workspace grant and writes through the same setForGroup as every other path.
The reader resolver never rejects a request: an exception is caught, logged as a warning, and yields an anonymous reader.
The catalogue is loaded in onApplicationBootstrap; an unreadable catalogue aborts the start. Every write to the directory reloads the catalogue in full.
All three virtual filter fields' subqueries are workspace-scoped, and there is no negation among their operators.
@orthacms/segments-domain has no dependencies at all, and the audience-field validation rules are read from it by both the admin form and the server DTO.
A content type with no id column makes SegmentReadScope throw rather than silently omit the fragment.
The middlewares are registered on {*splat} (Express 5 / path-to-regexp 8), and PrincipalMiddleware never short-circuits.
The application has exactly one layout contributor, and it is shell. A second one registered earlier disables authorization for every private route.
The layout is precisely AuthProvider on the outside, RequireAuth inside it, AppShell at the centre. Swapping the provider and the gate makes the gate blind.
No shell route carries public: true. The home page is private, as is the catch-all redirect, which is also mounted inside the layout.
Shell imports no feature plugin. Extension happens only through slots, the area override and the portals.
All contributions are registered before the first render and from scratch (_reset in a separate pass), so hot reloading does not double the sidebar's contents.
getItems() returns a copy: a consumer that sorts or filters in place does not spoil the list for the next one.
The order inside a slot is byOrder, stably; on equal order, the plugin registration order decides.
A navigation row without a permission is visible to everyone signed in; a row with a permission only to a holder of that key. The rule is the same in the sidebar and in the palette.
useHasPermission is called unconditionally (with '' when the field is absent), so that the hook order does not depend on slot data.
A navigation group is not rendered if no rows survive the permission filter — a heading never hangs over emptiness.
The sidebar's contextual area holds exactly one node; clearContent is a no-op if the caller is no longer the owner.
An overriding node brings its own named landmark: <nav aria-label="Primary"> belongs to GlobalSidebar and leaves with it.
The sidebar footer lives outside the contextual area and survives any override — it is the only region guaranteed to be mounted in both contexts.
useSidebarContent takes a factory + deps; raw JSX would be recreated every render and loop the effect. deps must list every field the node renders.
Both fillable areas are filled with createPortal rather than by handing a node to shell — otherwise the content loses its page's context.
Both portal hosts are always mounted, filled or not; a collapsed right panel does not unmount its filler or re-fetch its data.
The right panel exists exactly when there is at least one registration; at zero, the column is zero-width and inert.
Any toggle of the panel hands focus to the surviving half of the toggle — in both directions. A handoff on collapse only does not count.
An unclaimed focus handoff expires on the next tick and cannot be picked up by the next control to mount.
The panel's animation is gated on animate, which only toggle arms: neither the first frame nor a page registering the panel causes movement.
On a narrow viewport (a MOBILE_QUERY match) the panel starts collapsed regardless of storage, and that state is not written back.
The mobile overlay's Esc handler excludes the panel itself from the “is anything stacked above” check — otherwise it yields to itself.
The overlay's scrim is an aria-hidden decoration, not a <button>: a control unreachable from the keyboard is worse than no control at all.
SidebarToggle is a direct sibling of <main>; a wrapper breaks the [main:has([data-slot=top-bar])~&]:hidden selector and brings the floating button back to pages with a bar.
The skip link is the document's first focusable element, and its target is focusable (tabIndex={-1}).
The global chords (⌘K, ⌘B, ⌘J) do not fire in an input field or in contenteditable; a single shared function performs the check.
The palette restores focus when closed without navigating and deliberately does not restore it when navigating.
The active row is marked both visually and via aria-current="page"; only the root route has end: true.
Every label the design system exposes as a prop really is passed and translated — mobileTitle, mobileDescription, label, scrollLabel.
Every read from and write to cookies / localStorage / sessionStorage is wrapped in try/catch; a storage failure degrades to in-memory state, not to an error.
A route sets the tab title through useDocumentTitle and clears it on unmount; the unread badge is applied by a decorator, not by writing to document.title.
There is exactly one <main> in the document — both the skip link and RouteAnnouncer's scope depend on it.
A tool call is authorized in exactly one place — ToolRegistry.call, before dispatch. No handler checks its own requires.
visibleTo() and forSurface() are convenience filters; either can be removed without losing security, the check in call() cannot.
All keys in requires are required; the check is an exact match against the grantedPermissions set.
Permissions are never re-derived inside the package: createToolContext receives a ready-made set from whoever authenticated the caller.
ToolActor.userId is used only for attribution and never for authorization; for a token, the issuing user's role is not consulted at all.
A tool with no surfaces field is offered to both surfaces; surfaces: [] is impossible — the application will not start.
call() applies the same surface narrowing as forSurface(): calling another surface's tool answers “unknown tool”.
ToolContext.surface is set by call(), not by the caller; it is always the surface the call was authorized against.
surface may change only the presentation of a response, and never the set of checks, a filter, or which fields are disclosed.
An unknown name (404) and a forbidden name (403) are different answers; the refusal names the missing keys.
For data the answer is uniform: a content type that was not granted answers the same as one that does not exist, on both surfaces.
Authorization happens before argument validation: an unauthorized caller gets the same answer whatever it sends.
A missing arguments object is treated as {} by the registry, not by each consumer separately.
A resource passes through the same gate: a declared requires both hides the resource from the list and rejects a read of a directly named URI.

The application does not start on a duplicate name, a name that is not snake_case, an empty surfaces, an unknown permission in requires, or a non-object inputSchema. Every problem is reported at once.
register() is idempotent per provider instance; two different providers claiming the same name remain a wiring error.
ToolsModule is global, imported by both consumers and provided by neither; exactly one ToolRegistry exists in an application.
An application plugin injects ToolRegistry as @Optional(); a deployment with neither consumer boots, just without a catalogue.
Turning off MCP or the copilot removes only the corresponding routes and does not shrink the shared catalogue.
A non-HttpException goes out as an opaque 500 with the message hidden; the stack reaches the server log only.
Per-field issues from a 422 are carried into ToolError verbatim, under the same key.
The copilot's capability profile is not cached between runs, and permissions are re-checked once more before every call inside a run.
The first declaration of a name wins; a repeat lands in withheld rather than shadowing the earlier one.
The package owns no table, ships no migrations, and imports neither Drizzle, nor any vendor SDK, nor @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.
No type and no function in the package mentions HTTP, JSON-RPC or MCP.
The plugin owns no table and no migration; all it adds is two events in the shared outbox.
Every write goes through EntryWriterService. There is not one direct write to a content table.
The walk fetches only depths 0 and 1 in full; it does not follow outward from depth 1. Depth 2 exists in the document only as references.
A depth-1 entry's reference carries a resolvable $key, fetched by a projection over the identity columns, rather than somebody else's id alone.
The inverse side of a two-way relation is not exported, gets no CSV column and is not written on import. The owner's order is the order.
The export preflight runs the very same walk as the export: the numbers in the dialog are what will arrive.
The import's dry run and apply are one code path with a dryRun flag; the verdicts the preview showed describe what the apply will do.
A dry run writes not one row and not one byte.
The apply runs entirely in one transaction; blobs written by a failed run are deleted through ImportMediaRun, which belongs to the caller rather than to a singleton.
Entries are written values first, relations second, so a cycle and a mutual reference import correctly and the document's internal order means nothing.
The second pass starts from the exact value bag the first one wrote, and runs only if the relations actually changed — no second revision arises for one import.
A match is sought first by natural key, then by source row id, and both sides of the fingerprint read identityFor — the manifest's copy.
No match means a create under every one of the seven policies.
Depth 0 is governed only by ConflictPolicy and depth 1 only by RelationPolicy; neither setting acts on both.
link writes nothing to a matched related entry; only one with nothing to link to is created.
A skipped entry stays in the id map so references to it resolve.
A key with no fields is not indexed — otherwise it would collide with every other keyless entry of the type and link the unrelated.
The locale is part of the key fingerprint; en/hello and de/hello stay two rows.
The fingerprint is encoded as JSON, not joined with a separator.
One document's locale twins arrive in one translation group on the receiving side.
The package does not depend on @orthacms/i18n-server; the locale is read as an envelope column.
An import never exceeds the caller's permissions: content:create / content:update are re-checked per entry.
No operation crosses a workspace boundary: the request's workspace is stamped onto every write, and the manifest's sourceWorkspaceId is not read.
A type not granted to the workspace is indistinguishable from one that does not exist — the same 404.
An archive's central directory is read first; counts, sizes and the compression ratio are rejected before decompression.
A path escaping the archive root is rejected, not sanitised.
A document whose format version is above TRANSFER_FORMAT_VERSION is rejected rather than read “as best we can”.
The bytes decide an uploaded file's format; the file name and the declared format are a hint.
A non-UTF-8 file is rejected rather than imported as replacement characters.
A CSV column the type does not have is a hard rejection of the file naming that column, not a quiet skip.
A CSV media cell is never restored into an asset reference.
An asset's bytes are uploaded only when neither the source id nor the checksum found anything in this same workspace.
Asset bytes travel only in a ZIP; the capability table is the single source of that decision for both the server and the interface.
The export event is written before the response's first byte leaves.
An object missing from storage is a hole in the archive, not a failed export.
Assets are stored uncompressed in the archive, text members are deflated, and the timestamp is fixed — two exports of identical content match byte for byte.
The transfer-domain layer reads no clock and no database and imports neither NestJS, Drizzle nor React; its one dependency is @orthacms/content-domain.
The plugin's module is not global and exports nothing: the dependency arrow points only away from transfer.
An empty export selection is rejected; “empty means everything” does not exist in the API.
Changing the file or either of the two policies clears the verdict table.
After an import the cache of every type named in the verdicts is refreshed, plus the collection's type, plus the media library.

There is always at least one active administrator in the system: the last one can be neither demoted nor disabled. The check runs against a counter read under a global advisory lock taken when the aggregate is loaded.
A member cannot disable themselves and cannot change their own role. They can rename themselves.
Disabling and revoking sessions commit in one transaction: there is no “disabled but the sessions are alive” state, nor the reverse.
A user has at most one live invitation token and at most one reset token at a time. This is ensured by a delete+insert pair under a per-user lock.
The raw token is returned by exactly three routes (inviting, resending, issuing a reset) and exactly once. No read carries it.
Rotating a token sooner than 60 s is rejected with a 409 carrying a retryAfterSeconds; the check runs inside the same lock as the rotation itself.
Through this API only a row with the pending status can be deleted. A real account is never deleted.
A reset link is issued only to a member with the active status; pending and disabled are a 409.
Resending an invitation is possible only for pending; disabling only for active; re-enabling only for disabled.
An address is unique case-insensitively; the guarantee is a unique index on lower(email), not a check in the code.
A member's name, when set, cannot be empty or made of spaces: both DTOs trim the value before validation.
Every mutating route is closed by OriginGuard and every route by PermissionsGuard with a permission constant; the package has no public routes.
The package owns no table and ships no migrations; every write goes into a table migrated by identity or workspaces.
Every state change raises exactly one event of the corresponding kind into the transactional outbox, with the actor attached, in the same transaction as the write.
The domain/ layer imports neither @nestjs/* nor drizzle-orm nor class-validator nor infrastructure/.
The isLastAdmin flag is advisory: it affects only the state of controls, and its divergence from reality cannot lead to a violation of I-01.
The copilot tool answers with only the members of the current run's workspace and returns neither tokens nor session data.
The module is not global and exports nothing from DI: none of the package's providers is available to its neighbours.
The leaf does not import its consumers. Neither utils-admin nor utils-server depends on any plugin or any host. The only internal dependency is admin's @orthacms/design-system.
The packages contain no user-facing strings. Not one piece of text a human will see, and no react-intl. The copy is brought by whoever mounts it.
Neither package owns tables, routes or permissions. Zero migrations, zero controllers, zero permission keys.
One axios per application. A plugin does not create its own instance and does not import axios directly for requests to its own API.
X-Workspace-Id is set only when a workspace is set. Outside a workspace there is no header at all, not an empty string.
The 401 exemptions are matched on whole path segments of the normalized request — never with a bare startsWith over the string the caller passed.
The interceptor always re-throws the original error. The handler is a side effect; its exception is logged and does not replace the failure the caller sees.
The transport does not decide what a status means. The package has not one branch of the form “401 means a wrong password”.
ApiError.status === null means “there was no response”. That is the only way to tell a network failure from a server answer, and the retry predicate leans on exactly that.
4xx is not retried, except 408 and 429. Network failures and 5xx are retried, at most three times.
getItems() returns a copy. The internal array never leaves.
_reset() zeroes the length rather than re-creating the array — otherwise the getItems/_register closures stay on the old one.
Wiring is idempotent. Calling wireSlotContributions again with the same input gives the same result rather than a doubled one.
The reset is a separate pass over the distinct slots, before the registration loop.
byOrder does not sort in place.
Confirming a departure does not clear other keys. Each form drops its own on unmount.
Confirmed navigation goes through the router (useNavigate), not through history.pushState plus a synthetic popstate.
The click interception does not call stopPropagation() — only preventDefault().
The guard degrades to “no guard” outside the provider rather than throwing: useUnsavedChangesApi() returns null.
The tab title is assembled, not appended to. The decorator is a transformation over a freshly assembled string; nobody writes to document.title around render().
The schema is the security boundary. Only what is listed in fields/relations reaches the SQL; everything else is a 400.
Every lookup of a user-supplied name in a map goes through own() (or a direct Object.hasOwn), never through bare bracket notation.
A leaf's value is a scalar. null, a missing key, an object and an array give a 400; String(v) is never applied to them.
The operator is checked against the field's type, not only against the vocabulary — and before the value is coerced.
A negation on a relation path is NOT EXISTS(… the positive form …), wrapped around the outermost hop.
A negation on an ordinary column includes NULL.
scope is glued inside the EXISTS, and when it is present the many-to-many fast path by id is disabled.
Parent columns are re-resolved by rebind against the table the translator is querying; a one-to-many's target fk never is.
No value that arrived over the wire reaches sql.raw. The interval's unit is chosen by a switch over three constants.

An untranslatable schema is a 500 (FilterSchemaException), not a 400. Every default: in a switch throws rather than returning undefined: an undefined predicate silently drops out of and()/or() and widens the result set.
An empty in/nin is rejected — otherwise the filter silently means “nothing” or “everything”.
context does not overwrite the error envelope: the service keys are written after the context is spread.
The fan-out subscriber performs no network I/O. It runs one SELECT and one batched INSERT and returns — it is called inside the dispatcher's claim transaction.
A delivery's claim is committed before the HTTP request is made. No database transaction is open while a receiver is answering.
An empty event_kinds, content_types or workspace set matches everything, including kinds, types and workspaces that do not exist yet.
An event with no workspace reaches only endpoints with all_workspaces = true.
An unknown event kind matches nothing. The subscriber declares the subscribable set, and ping is not in it.
event_id is stable across redeliveries; id (and therefore X-Ortha-Delivery) is not. The receiver deduplicates on the former.
The envelope inside payload is frozen at fan-out. A redelivery sends what happened, never what is true now.
The partial unique index makes fan-out idempotent: a redelivered outbox event cannot queue the same (endpoint, event) twice, while a manual resend is not blocked by it.
The plaintext secret is returned by exactly two routes — create and rotate — and by nothing else, ever.
The URL policy is applied at write time and at connect time, the second against the resolved address. Redirects are not followed.
A custom header may not begin with X-Ortha- nor name a transport header. Enforced on every write, not only in the UI.
4xx other than 408 and 429 is terminal; 5xx, 408, 429 and transport failures retry. Retry-After is honoured up to one hour.
Auto-disable increments the counter and flips enabled in one statement, so concurrent workers cannot both step over the threshold and leave the endpoint on.
Re-enabling an endpoint by hand clears disabled_reason and zeroes consecutive_failures: the reason on screen can never outlive the condition.
A disabled or deleted endpoint never receives a delivery that was queued before the switch — the worker re-reads it after claiming and closes the row instead.
claimTimeoutMs > timeoutMs is checked at boot. The plugin refuses to start otherwise.
The response snippet stored is capped at responseSnippetBytes.
Both permission keys are administrator-only, and the editor page requires webhooks:manage, not merely webhooks:read.
Permission and membership are checked independently, and both checks are mandatory: holding workspaces:update never opens access to a workspace the caller does not belong to.

Both guards delegate the decision to the single authorizeWorkspaceAccess function. One documented exception: media/server's download controller asks the same membership probe directly and answers 404 rather than 403, because it derives the workspace from the asset id and a 403 would confirm that the asset exists. So there is no second membership probe; there is one other call site, and it is deliberate.
“Not a member” and “no such workspace” are indistinguishable: the same 403 with the same text, on every route and on the shell's screen.
GET /api/workspaces returns only the caller's workspaces; no unscoped list exists in the read model.
Every route of the form /workspaces/:id/… carries WorkspaceMemberGuard — both preview counters included.
@CurrentWorkspace() either returns a verified identifier or throws; it never returns undefined.
A membership carries no role; a workspace has no owner, and the creator is simply the first member with no privileges.
The last member cannot be removed: LastMemberError → 409. The rule sits on the aggregate and is not bypassed by any path.
Every aggregate mutator is idempotent and returns whether anything changed; on false neither a row nor a domain event is written.
A slug is system-wide unique; the arbiter is the unique index, and its violation is translated into a 409, not a 500.
The slug format (lowercase Latin letters, digits, hyphen; 1–120) is checked by a value object rather than a DTO decorator, and identically on the server and in the admin UI.
A workspace's colour always belongs to the seven-key palette; an arbitrary value cannot be written.
A workspace's slug is immutable: the field is absent from UpdateWorkspaceDto, and there is no other way to change it.
A workspace cannot be deleted while it holds content entries (409); a grant cannot be revoked while the type has entries in that workspace (409).
If the entry counter is not bound, destructive operations refuse (503), while the reading counters keep answering 0.
Deletion and grant revocation load the aggregate under the workspace's exclusive advisory lock; writing an entry takes the shared one.
Every purger runs inside the delete transaction and sequentially; a thrown exception rolls the whole deletion back.
Non-transactional resource reclamation runs only after the commit, and its failure is logged and swallowed.
Registering a purger with the same purgeName twice is an exception, not a silent overwrite.
A content type's kind (collection or single) is derived by the server from the catalogue; the client sends only a slug, and an unknown slug gives a 400.
An “all content” grant is expanded into explicit rows per known slug: the presence of a row always means an explicit grant.
Every state change puts its domain event into the outbox in the same transaction; there are no inline calls to the audit recorder.
domain/ imports neither @nestjs/* nor drizzle-orm nor class-validator nor infrastructure/.
The users stub from external-refs.ts is not re-exported from schema/index.ts, so drizzle-kit emits no second CREATE TABLE users.
Invited members are matched by normalised address; one address in different cases yields one account, not two.
A user identifier that does not resolve to a real users row is discarded and does not bring workspace creation down.
WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY answers the question of existence, not of status: an archived workspace is a legitimate API-token scope.
Purging a token's scopes does not revoke the token itself.
The slug-availability check requires workspaces:create; authentication is not enough.
Every preview counter is gated on the same permission as the action it guards.
In the admin UI a failure to load the list is never displayed as “there are no workspaces”.
The dialog's destructive button is enabled only on a known zero count; both “checking” and “the check failed” block it.
A failed slug check yields the Unknown state and does not unlock the move to the next step.
Danger zone is gated on both the tab and the route: a direct link without the permission redirects to general with an explanation.
The plugin contributes no route, no navigation item and no layout: the object WysiwygPlugin() returns holds only name and slots.
The editor claims every richtext field except those with admin.widget === 'textarea'. There is no other condition in isWysiwygField.
src/index.ts exports neither the preview, nor the editor, nor anything that statically pulls in TipTap; both halves of the contribution are taken through React.lazy.
The preview never renders stored markup as is: the value always goes through the editor's own ProseMirror schema (renderRichText), and a legacy string through an inert DOMParser.
The preview is left with not one focusable element: links are flattened into <span data-link>. That is the correctness condition for the button lying over it.
The collapsed field's button carries the field's id and an aria-describedby, but neither aria-invalid nor aria-required.
Unfolding replaces the working area's content rather than opening a dialog: the sidebar, the entry heading, the Save/Publish buttons and the properties panel stay mounted and operable.
At most one field is unfolded at a time; the state is held by EntryEditor, and the control only asks.
The editor panel is mounted only while the field is unfolded, and is seeded from the value once, at mount; there is no controlled content synchronisation.
The editor has no Save and no Cancel of its own: every edit is written into the entry's form through onChange, and the only commit boundary is the entry's Save.
An empty document is stored as null rather than as a document with an empty paragraph; a meaningful document is handed to the form verbatim.
Emptiness is defined by the core (isEmptyRichText) as a list of what emptiness is (doc, paragraph, hardBreak, whitespace text, container) rather than as the negation of a list of "meaningful" nodes.
The remarks list under the document is built by the core's inspectRichText: an error here is exactly what will refuse the save, and a warning exactly what will not.
A language tag is checked by the core's isWellFormedLanguageTag, so the editor cannot accept a tag the save will later reject.
The language mark is not a textStyle: "Clear formatting" does not remove it.
Every <th> this editor can produce carries scope="col", and the attribute travels into the preview and the published body alike (set through HTMLAttributes, not by overriding renderHTML).
Tab in a table's last cell adds a row once; pressing it again in the remaining empty row falls through and releases focus.
Reducing the column count never deletes content: the discarded columns' blocks move into the last remaining one.
The column count is always within 2..4 — on insert and when parsing foreign markup alike (clampCount handles NaN).
Choosing a second callout tone recolours the current one rather than nesting a callout inside a callout.

A media node's src is checked twice — in the dialog (to explain it to the author) and in the node, on insert and on parse (to protect the stored content). Only http(s) and same-origin paths are allowed; a protocol-relative //host/… is rejected.
An unsafe embed is skipped rather than saved as a broken node; an with an inadmissible src is not imported at all rather than imported with an empty src.
Media size is stored in the width attribute; a height is never stored; a width below 64px reads as "no width chosen" rather than being clamped upward.
Media alignment is stored in data-align and applied with margins; the value left is not written; the alignment menu for media has no "Justify" item.
Ticking "decorative" clears the alt: a non-empty alt together with data-decorative is impossible in the saved HTML.
Inside the editor an image with no alt gets a fallback accessible name; the saved HTML carries the real value, empty included.
Every <form> in a popup in this package calls stopPropagation() on its submit; the entry is never saved from a popup under any circumstances.
Every popup opened from a dropdown menu (media sources, the language dialog, the "by URL" dialogs) is mounted by the toolbar, not by the menu item.
Every toolbar control does preventDefault on mousedown, so a press never collapses the selection the command works on.
No editor-state selector is called through useEditorState directly: they all go through useLiveEditorState, which returns whenGone on a destroyed editor.
In readOnly mode the toolbar is not mounted at all, onUpdate does not write into the form, focus is not set, and the surface's role is region.
A paste loses color, font-size and background-color; a colour applied by a toolbar command does not.
The domain/ layer imports neither React nor TipTap; the media node view sits next to its extension so that infrastructure/ does not import upwards into presentation/.
Every style rule in the package hangs off .ortha-wysiwyg: none can reach the rest of the admin UI, and the editor surface and the preview render the same markup identically.
Not one admin class name reaches the stored content: the custom nodes serialise into data- attributes.
The unfolded view declares a lang only for a field marked localized, and never for a shared one.
Leaving the unfolded view returns focus to the field's button (through a requestAnimationFrame) rather than dropping it onto <body>.
editorExtensions holds no second copy of an extension StarterKit already brings (Link, Underline, TrailingNode): a duplicate name makes TipTap warn and resolve the extension set unpredictably.
